nodes.title: Musculoskeletal system
nodes.summary: Muscle, bone, tendon and the control system that keeps you upright. The system whose decline is most visible in old age and most modifiable at any age.
citations: Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position
US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)
EWGSOP2 sarcopenia consensus (2019)

nodes.title: Muscular strength
nodes.summary: Maximal force the muscles can produce. Falls roughly 1-1.5% per year from midlife, faster than muscle mass itself, and predicts disability independently of mass.
citations: Cochrane - progressive resistance training in older adults (2009)
EWGSOP2 sarcopenia consensus (2019)
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position

nodes.title: Lean muscle mass
nodes.summary: The quantity of contractile tissue. A metabolic reservoir as well as a mechanical one - low lean mass tracks with worse outcomes after illness, surgery and injury.
citations: EWGSOP2 sarcopenia consensus (2019)
ISSN position stand - protein and exercise (2017)
ISCD official positions on DXA (2019)

nodes.title: Bone mineral density
nodes.summary: Skeletal mass and architecture. Bone responds to strain, not to activity in general, which is why loading matters more than time spent moving.

attrs.decline_onset: after peak bone mass ~age 30; sharp post-menopause

citations: Bone Health and Osteoporosis Foundation Clinician's Guide (2022)
ISCD official positions on DXA (2019)

nodes.title: Stability and balance
nodes.summary: The ability to keep the centre of mass over the base of support and recover when it leaves. The function standing between an older adult and the fall that ends independence.
citations: Cochrane - exercise for preventing falls in older people (2019)
USPSTF falls prevention in community-dwelling older adults (2018)
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position

nodes.title: Joint mobility
nodes.summary: Usable range of motion under control. Distinct from passive flexibility - the question is whether you can reach a position and produce force there.
citations: AAOS goniometric range-of-motion normative values
NICE NG226 osteoarthritis in over 16s (2022)

nodes.title: Tendon and connective tissue capacity
nodes.summary: How much repeated load tendon can absorb before it becomes symptomatic. Adapts far more slowly than muscle, which is the usual reason training progressions fail.
citations: Cook and Purdam tendon pathology continuum model (2009)
JOSPT clinical practice guideline - Achilles tendinopathy (2018)

nodes.title: Freedom from falls
nodes.summary: Reaching late life without a fall that fractures a hip, causes a head injury, or starts the confidence spiral that ends in a care home. A cliff-edge outcome, not a gradual one.

attrs.why_it_matters: one hip fracture at 80 frequently ends independent living outright

citations: USPSTF falls prevention in community-dwelling older adults (2018)
Cochrane - exercise for preventing falls in older people (2019)
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position

nodes.title: Bone stress injury
nodes.summary: A stress reaction or stress fracture from repetitive loading outpacing bone remodelling. Typically 6-12 weeks of lost training and a hard reset of aerobic progress.
citations: Consensus statements on bone stress injury in athletes
Bone Health and Osteoporosis Foundation Clinician's Guide (2022)

nodes.title: Overuse tendinopathy
nodes.summary: Load-related tendon pain and stiffness from volume rising faster than tendon adaptation. Slow to settle and prone to recurrence when the underlying progression error is not fixed.

attrs.typical_sites: Achilles, patellar, gluteal, rotator cuff, elbow extensors

citations: Cook and Purdam tendon pathology continuum model (2009)
JOSPT clinical practice guideline - Achilles tendinopathy (2018)

nodes.title: Acute back injury or flare
nodes.summary: A sudden episode of disabling back pain, usually from a loaded lift with a load or technique the trunk was not prepared for. Mostly self-limiting, but a common reason people abandon training entirely.

attrs.note: imaging findings correlate poorly with pain; most episodes settle without them

citations: NICE NG59 low back pain and sciatica

nodes.title: Resistance training
nodes.summary: Progressive loading of the major movement patterns two to three times a week. The single highest-yield musculoskeletal intervention and the one most often skipped in favour of cardio.

attrs.modality: free weights, machines, bands or bodyweight
attrs.equipment_floor: bands and bodyweight are sufficient to start

citations: ACSM Position Stand 2011 - quantity and quality of exercise
Cochrane - progressive resistance training in older adults (2009)
US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position

nodes.title: Posterior chain strengthening
nodes.summary: Deliberate loading of glutes, hamstrings and spinal extensors through hinge patterns. The base that makes running, carrying and lifting tolerable for a back that has been painful.

attrs.examples: hip hinge, Romanian deadlift, hip thrust, back extension

citations: NICE NG59 low back pain and sciatica
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

nodes.title: Grip strength training
nodes.summary: Direct loading of the hands and forearms via hangs, holds and thick-bar work. Grip is a cheap window onto whole-body strength and tracks with mortality across populations.

attrs.examples: dead hangs, timed holds, towel or thick-bar work

citations: Leong et al., Lancet (2015) - PURE grip strength and mortality
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position
Roberts et al. - standardised protocol for grip strength measurement

nodes.title: Loaded carries
nodes.summary: Walking under load held at the sides or overhead. Trains grip, trunk and gait simultaneously and maps directly onto carrying shopping up a flight of stairs at 85.

attrs.examples: farmer carry, suitcase carry, overhead carry

citations: Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position
Knapik et al. - load carriage physiology and injury, Military Medicine
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

nodes.title: Calf and plantar loading
nodes.summary: Progressive heel raises and plantar fascia loading, held under tension rather than bounced. The mainstay of both plantar heel pain rehabilitation and prevention of recurrence.

attrs.examples: straight and bent-knee heel raises, high-load plantar fascia work
attrs.frequency: most days, then 3 per week for maintenance

citations: JOSPT clinical practice guideline - heel pain and plantar fasciitis (2023)
Alfredson eccentric calf loading protocol (1998)

nodes.title: Quadriceps strengthening
nodes.summary: Targeted loading of the knee extensors. The best-supported non-drug intervention for knee osteoarthritis pain and function, and quietly one of the strongest fall-prevention levers.

attrs.examples: leg press, split squat, step-up, seated knee extension

citations: Cochrane - exercise for knee osteoarthritis (2015)
OARSI non-surgical management of knee osteoarthritis (2019)
NICE NG226 osteoarthritis in over 16s (2022)

nodes.title: Trunk stability training
nodes.summary: Anti-extension, anti-rotation and anti-lateral-flexion work that teaches the trunk to resist movement under load rather than produce it.

attrs.examples: dead bug, plank variants, Pallof press, side plank

citations: NICE NG59 low back pain and sciatica
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

nodes.title: Balance training
nodes.summary: Specific practice of narrowed-base, single-leg and perturbed standing. Balance is trainable at any age and does not improve as a side effect of walking or cycling.

attrs.examples: single-leg stance, tandem walking, reactive step training
attrs.frequency: 3 or more sessions per week, short doses

citations: Cochrane - exercise for preventing falls in older people (2019)
USPSTF falls prevention in community-dwelling older adults (2018)
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position

nodes.title: Plyometric and impact loading
nodes.summary: Brief bouts of hopping, jumping and landing. The strain rate, not the volume, is what bone responds to - a few dozen good jumps beats an hour of low-strain movement.

attrs.examples: hops, drop jumps, skipping, low-box landings
attrs.volume: tens rather than hundreds of contacts

citations: Bone Health and Osteoporosis Foundation Clinician's Guide (2022)
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

nodes.title: Hip mobility work
nodes.summary: Loaded and end-range hip work to keep internal rotation, extension and flexion usable. Hip range loss shows up first as compensation elsewhere, usually the lower back.

attrs.examples: 90/90 transitions, hip airplanes, deep split-squat holds

citations: AAOS goniometric range-of-motion normative values
NICE NG226 osteoarthritis in over 16s (2022)

nodes.title: Eccentric loading
nodes.summary: Slow lengthening contractions under load. The best-established mechanical stimulus for remodelling a painful tendon and for building tolerance to downhill and deceleration work.

attrs.examples: Alfredson-style heel drops, slow tempo lowering, Nordic curls
attrs.frequency: daily to every other day during rehabilitation

citations: Alfredson eccentric calf loading protocol (1998)
JOSPT clinical practice guideline - Achilles tendinopathy (2018)
Cook and Purdam tendon pathology continuum model (2009)

nodes.title: Footwear selection
nodes.summary: Choosing shoes by fit, stack and how they feel over a real run rather than by category label. Evidence for prescriptive matching of shoe type to foot type is weak; comfort filtering has better support.

attrs.note: comfort-based selection has more support than motion-control prescription
attrs.replacement: when cushioning or fit changes noticeably

citations: Cochrane and BJSM reviews of foot orthoses - findings mixed
JOSPT clinical practice guideline - heel pain and plantar fasciitis (2023)

nodes.title: Training load management
nodes.summary: Progressing volume and intensity gradually, tracking how much changed week to week, and inserting easier weeks. The least glamorous injury-prevention lever and the most reliable one.

attrs.heuristic: raise one variable at a time; keep weekly jumps modest
attrs.note: the specific 10% rule is a convention, not a validated threshold

citations: BJSM consensus - return to running after injury
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

nodes.title: Heat acclimatisation
nodes.summary: Structured, progressive exposure to exercising in heat over roughly ten to fourteen days. Produces real physiological adaptation - plasma volume, sweat onset, sweat sodium - not just tolerance.

attrs.protocol: 10-14 consecutive days of gradually lengthening heat exposure
attrs.decay: adaptation fades within 2-4 weeks without exposure

citations: ACSM Position Stand - exertional heat illness (2007)
NATA position statement - exertional heat illnesses (2015)

nodes.title: DEXA appendicular lean mass
nodes.summary: Whole-body composition scan reporting lean mass by region. The reference method for tracking muscle over years, and the only one precise enough to detect a real change in one person.
citations: ISCD official positions on DXA (2019)
EWGSOP2 sarcopenia consensus (2019)

nodes.title: DEXA bone mineral density
nodes.summary: Areal bone density at hip and spine, reported as T-score and Z-score. The measurement osteoporosis diagnosis is actually defined on.
citations: ISCD official positions on DXA (2019)
Bone Health and Osteoporosis Foundation Clinician's Guide (2022)

nodes.title: Tendon ultrasound
nodes.summary: Imaging of tendon thickness and structure. Useful for confirming a structural picture, but poorly correlated with pain - abnormal tendons are common in people with no symptoms.

attrs.caveat: structure and symptoms diverge often

citations: Ultrasound tendon imaging reliability literature
Cook and Purdam tendon pathology continuum model (2009)

nodes.title: Grip strength (dynamometer)
nodes.summary: Maximal isometric hand grip on a calibrated dynamometer. Cheap, fast, standardised, and one of the better-validated single predictors of mortality and disability.

attrs.protocol_sensitivity: posture and elbow angle must be fixed between tests

citations: Leong et al., Lancet (2015) - PURE grip strength and mortality
Roberts et al. - standardised protocol for grip strength measurement
EWGSOP2 sarcopenia consensus (2019)

nodes.title: Estimated one-rep max
nodes.summary: Strength inferred from a set taken near failure at a submaximal load. Good for tracking one person over time; the prediction equations drift at very high or very low rep counts.
citations: Brzycki and Epley 1RM prediction equations - validation literature
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

nodes.title: Five-times sit-to-stand
nodes.summary: Time to rise from a chair five times without using the arms. Captures leg power, balance and confidence at once, and needs nothing but a chair and a stopwatch.
citations: Bohannon - five-times sit-to-stand reference values
Guralnik et al. - Short Physical Performance Battery (1994)

nodes.title: Usual gait speed
nodes.summary: Comfortable walking speed over a measured short course. A remarkably strong summary signal in older adults - it aggregates strength, balance, cardiorespiratory reserve and neurological status.
citations: Studenski et al., JAMA (2011) - gait speed and survival
Guralnik et al. - Short Physical Performance Battery (1994)

nodes.title: Single-leg stance time
nodes.summary: How long you can stand on one leg, eyes open and then closed. Declines steeply with age and is the most direct available proxy for the function that prevents falls.
citations: Springer et al. - single-leg stance normative data by age
Cochrane - exercise for preventing falls in older people (2019)

nodes.title: Countermovement jump height
nodes.summary: Jump height from a standing countermovement. A power measure rather than a strength measure, and power declines earlier and faster with age than maximal force does.
citations: Countermovement jump reliability and normative data - sports science literature

nodes.title: Single-leg heel raise repetitions
nodes.summary: Repetitions of a single-leg heel raise to fatigue through full range. The standard functional test of calf and Achilles capacity, and a sensible return-to-running gate.
citations: Hebert-Losier et al. - heel-rise test normative data
JOSPT clinical practice guideline - Achilles tendinopathy (2018)

nodes.title: Hip range of motion (goniometry)
nodes.summary: Measured hip flexion, extension and internal rotation. Reasonably repeatable when the same person measures with the same protocol; between-rater agreement is weaker.
citations: AAOS goniometric range-of-motion normative values

nodes.title: Bioimpedance lean mass
nodes.summary: Consumer scale or handheld estimate of body composition from electrical impedance. Sensitive to hydration and time of day - readable as a trend under fixed conditions, not as an absolute number.

attrs.caveat: absolute values disagree with DEXA by several kg

citations: Consumer bioimpedance versus DXA agreement studies

nodes.title: Wearable step count
nodes.summary: Daily steps from a phone or watch. A decent proxy for overall movement volume, a poor one for loading intensity - it cannot tell a heavy carry from a stroll.
citations: Consumer step-count accuracy validation studies

nodes.title: Running cadence
nodes.summary: Steps per minute while running, from a watch or foot pod. Related to stride length and impact loading, but the popular universal target is not supported for every runner.

attrs.caveat: no single optimal cadence across runners

citations: Running cadence and impact loading - biomechanics literature

nodes.title: Pain rating (self-report)
nodes.summary: A 0-10 numeric rating of pain, ideally recorded in a fixed context such as first steps in the morning. Subjective and noisy, but it is the outcome that actually matters to the person.
citations: Hawker et al. (2011) - measurement properties of pain rating scales

nodes.title: Session rating of perceived exertion
nodes.summary: How hard a session felt, on the Borg or 0-10 scale. Cheap load-monitoring input; it drifts with mood, sleep and caffeine, so it is a trend signal rather than a measurement.
citations: Borg RPE scale validation literature

nodes.title: Low lean muscle mass
nodes.summary: Appendicular lean mass index below the sarcopenia cut-point for age and sex. Sharpens the case for resistance training and protein rather than blocking anything.
citations: EWGSOP2 sarcopenia consensus (2019)
ISCD official positions on DXA (2019)

nodes.title: Low grip strength
nodes.summary: Grip below the age and sex reference range. Rarely a hand problem - it is usually a whole-body strength signal, and it predicts hard outcomes.
citations: Leong et al., Lancet (2015) - PURE grip strength and mortality
EWGSOP2 sarcopenia consensus (2019)

nodes.title: Low bone density (osteopenia range)
nodes.summary: DEXA T-score between -1.0 and -2.5. Not a diagnosis of osteoporosis, but the point at which loading and fall prevention stop being optional.
citations: Bone Health and Osteoporosis Foundation Clinician's Guide (2022)
ISCD official positions on DXA (2019)

nodes.title: Prior fall in the last 12 months
nodes.summary: One of the strongest single predictors of the next fall. Turns balance work from a general recommendation into a specific priority.

attrs.note: also a FRAX-relevant fracture risk input

citations: USPSTF falls prevention in community-dwelling older adults (2018)
Kanis et al. - FRAX and prior falls as fracture risk input

nodes.title: Chronic low back pain
nodes.summary: Back pain persisting beyond three months without a red-flag cause. Activity is part of the treatment, not a risk to be avoided - but the order in which activity is reintroduced matters.

attrs.typical_course: fluctuating; flares do not mean damage

citations: NICE NG59 low back pain and sciatica

nodes.title: Plantar heel pain (plantar fasciitis)
nodes.summary: Load-related pain under the heel, classically worst on the first steps of the morning. Slow to settle, and the usual driver is a volume increase the tissue was not ready for.
citations: JOSPT clinical practice guideline - heel pain and plantar fasciitis (2023)

nodes.title: Flat feet / pes planus
nodes.summary: A low or absent medial arch. Extremely common and mostly asymptomatic - on its own it is a footwear and progression consideration, not a reason to avoid impact.

attrs.note: poor predictor of injury in isolation

citations: Cochrane and BJSM reviews of foot orthoses - findings mixed

nodes.title: Knee osteoarthritis
nodes.summary: Degenerative knee joint change with pain and stiffness. The most consequential misconception in this whole graph is that it rules out running - the evidence does not support that.

attrs.misconception_corrected: recreational running is not shown to accelerate knee OA; sedentary and elite-volume groups differ from recreational runners

citations: NICE NG226 osteoarthritis in over 16s (2022)
OARSI non-surgical management of knee osteoarthritis (2019)
Cochrane - exercise for knee osteoarthritis (2015)
ACR/Arthritis Foundation osteoarthritis guideline (2019)

nodes.title: Hip osteoarthritis
nodes.summary: Degenerative hip change, usually felt as groin pain and lost internal rotation. Exercise therapy is first-line here too, with range work alongside strengthening.
citations: NICE NG226 osteoarthritis in over 16s (2022)
OARSI non-surgical management of knee osteoarthritis (2019)

nodes.title: Shoulder impingement / subacromial pain
nodes.summary: Pain in the outer shoulder on overhead and reaching movement. Overhead loading is modified rather than removed - complete rest tends to prolong it.

attrs.aggravators: repeated overhead reaching, pressing, freestyle swimming volume

citations: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

nodes.title: Achilles tendinopathy
nodes.summary: Load-related pain and stiffness in the Achilles tendon. Responds to progressive loading; responds badly to rest followed by an abrupt return to previous volume.

attrs.hallmark: morning stiffness, pain warming up then returning after activity

citations: JOSPT clinical practice guideline - Achilles tendinopathy (2018)
Alfredson eccentric calf loading protocol (1998)
Cook and Purdam tendon pathology continuum model (2009)

nodes.title: Osteoporosis
nodes.summary: Bone density at or below a T-score of -2.5, or a prior fragility fracture. Loading and balance work become more important, while loaded spinal flexion becomes the thing to design around.

attrs.key_avoidance: heavily loaded end-range spinal flexion and twisting

citations: Bone Health and Osteoporosis Foundation Clinician's Guide (2022)
ISCD official positions on DXA (2019)

nodes.title: Osteopenia
nodes.summary: Bone density between -1.0 and -2.5. The window where loading changes the trajectory, and where doing nothing is the actual risk.
citations: Bone Health and Osteoporosis Foundation Clinician's Guide (2022)

nodes.title: Obesity
nodes.summary: Body mass sufficient to change joint loading, thermoregulation and exercise tolerance. Reshapes how activity is introduced; almost never a reason to withhold it.

attrs.considerations: joint load, heat dissipation, starting capacity, chafing and skin integrity

citations: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)
US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)

nodes.title: Asthma
nodes.summary: Reversible airway narrowing, often provoked by exercise, cold dry air, or high ventilation rates. Well-controlled asthma is compatible with essentially all training.

attrs.triggers: cold dry air, high ventilation, allergens
attrs.note: reliever inhaler available before sessions

citations: GINA global strategy for asthma management (2024)

nodes.title: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
nodes.summary: Acid reflux provoked by position, meal timing and intra-abdominal pressure. Mostly a timing and technique modifier rather than an exercise-selection one.

attrs.aggravators: supine positions, heavy Valsalva, exercising soon after eating, late meals

citations: ACG clinical guideline - GERD (2022)

nodes.title: Atrial fibrillation
nodes.summary: Irregular atrial rhythm, paroxysmal or persistent. Two practical consequences: heart-rate-based intensity targets stop meaning anything, and unsupervised open water gets riskier.

attrs.key_consequence: heart rate is not a usable intensity signal during AF
attrs.management_context: assumes rate/rhythm control and anticoagulation decisions are already handled clinically

citations: ESC atrial fibrillation guideline (2024)

nodes.title: Uncontrolled hypertension
nodes.summary: Blood pressure persistently above target despite treatment, or untreated. Maximal-effort and heavy Valsalva work waits until it is controlled; walking does not.

attrs.threshold_context: resting BP repeatedly at or above 180/110 warrants deferring high-intensity work

citations: ACC/AHA hypertension guideline (2017)
AHA scientific statement - resistance exercise and cardiovascular disease (2007)

nodes.title: Early chronic kidney disease
nodes.summary: Reduced kidney function at stage G1-G3. Changes protein targets and hydration planning; exercise itself remains clearly beneficial.

attrs.note: protein targets should be set with the treating clinician, not from a general athletic recommendation

citations: KDIGO CKD guideline (2024)

nodes.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea
nodes.summary: Repeated airway collapse in sleep, producing fragmentation and daytime fatigue. Depresses training tolerance and recovery quality until it is treated.

attrs.consequence: reduced recovery capacity, blunted training response, daytime sleepiness

citations: AASM/AHA scientific statement - obstructive sleep apnoea (2021)

nodes.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome
nodes.summary: An endocrine and metabolic syndrome with insulin resistance in the majority. Sharpens the case for resistance training and regular movement.

attrs.metabolic_note: insulin resistance common independent of body weight

citations: International evidence-based PCOS guideline (2023)

nodes.title: Gout
nodes.summary: Crystal arthropathy with acute, extremely painful flares. Between flares, training is normal; during one, loading the affected joint is not.

attrs.flare_state: acute flares are transient - this modifier should be time-boxed, not permanent

citations: ACR gout management guideline (2020)

nodes.title: Migraine
nodes.summary: Recurrent disabling headache with common triggers in sleep disruption, dehydration and abrupt intensity. Regular aerobic activity tends to reduce frequency over months.

attrs.triggers: sleep irregularity, dehydration, skipped meals, abrupt maximal effort, heat

citations: International Headache Society - secondary headache red flags

nodes.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
nodes.summary: Fat accumulation in the liver on a metabolic background. Both aerobic and resistance training reduce liver fat, partly independently of weight change.

attrs.note: liver fat falls with training even without large weight loss

citations: EASL-EASD-EASO MASLD clinical practice guideline (2024)

nodes.title: Depression or anxiety
nodes.summary: Mood or anxiety disorder affecting motivation, energy and follow-through. The adherence axis dominates here: the plan that gets done beats the optimal plan.

attrs.planning_principle: reduce the activation cost of the first session, not the eventual dose

citations: Cochrane - exercise for depression (2013)

nodes.title: Hypothyroidism
nodes.summary: Underactive thyroid, treated or not. Untreated or under-replaced, it slows recovery, reduces exercise tolerance and can cause exertional muscle symptoms.

attrs.note: symptoms attributed to training may be replacement-dose related

citations: ATA guideline - hypothyroidism treatment (2014)

nodes.title: Heat sensitivity
nodes.summary: A person who tolerates exertional heat poorly - by history, medication, or prior heat illness. Individual vulnerability, distinct from the ambient conditions themselves.

attrs.causes: prior heat illness, anticholinergic or diuretic medication, poor acclimatisation state

citations: ACSM Position Stand - exertional heat illness (2007)
NATA position statement - exertional heat illnesses (2015)

nodes.title: Beginner or deconditioned
nodes.summary: Little recent training history. The dominant risk is not the exercise but the rate of progression into it, and the dominant failure is starting at a dose that cannot be repeated.

attrs.principle: the first eight weeks buy tolerance, not fitness

citations: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)
US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)

nodes.title: Older adult (65+)
nodes.summary: Age band where strength, power and balance decline steepen and where a fall stops being an inconvenience. Nothing is removed; priorities and progression rates change.

attrs.priority_shift: balance, power and protein move up the list

citations: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour (2020)
USPSTF falls prevention in community-dwelling older adults (2018)
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position

nodes.title: Pregnancy
nodes.summary: Physiological changes across trimesters affecting balance, core mechanics, thermoregulation and supine tolerance. Activity is recommended; a few specific things are not.

attrs.note: specific plans belong with the maternity care team

citations: ACOG Committee Opinion 804 - physical activity in pregnancy (2020)

nodes.title: Hot and humid conditions
nodes.summary: High wet-bulb conditions where evaporative cooling fails. The single environmental modifier most capable of turning an ordinary session into a medical emergency.

attrs.escalation: activity restriction thresholds rise as WBGT rises

citations: ACSM Position Stand - exertional heat illness (2007)
NATA position statement - exertional heat illnesses (2015)

nodes.title: Downhill-heavy terrain
nodes.summary: Routes with substantial sustained descent. Eccentric loading on the descent causes far more muscle damage and soreness than the same distance on the flat.

attrs.consequence: delayed soreness, temporary strength loss, higher injury risk when unaccustomed

citations: Sports Medicine review - eccentric exercise and exercise-induced muscle damage

nodes.title: High altitude
nodes.summary: Elevations above roughly 2,500 m. Reduced oxygen availability lowers sustainable intensity and adds an acute mountain sickness risk on rapid ascent.

attrs.ascent_rule: gradual ascent above 3,000 m sleeping altitude

citations: Wilderness Medical Society practice guidelines - acute altitude illness (2019)

nodes.title: Cold conditions
nodes.summary: Cold, wind and icy ground. The airway and clothing issues are manageable; the fall risk on ice is the part that gets underweighted.

attrs.risks: airway irritation, frostbite at extremes, slips on ice

citations: Wilderness Medical Society practice guidelines - cold injury (2019)

nodes.title: No gym access
nodes.summary: No membership or facility. Constrains equipment and external load, but almost nothing in the strength list actually requires a gym to start.

attrs.workarounds: bands, adjustable dumbbells, backpack load, bodyweight progressions

citations: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)
US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)

nodes.title: No pool access
nodes.summary: No usable pool. A hard constraint on swimming specifically, and the clearest case in the graph for a block that immediately offers substitutes.
citations: US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)

nodes.title: Limited time
nodes.summary: Realistically under about three hours a week for training. Forces explicit prioritisation, which usually means strength and short high-intensity work survive and long slow volume does not.

attrs.principle: protect the sessions with the steepest dose-response first

citations: US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position

nodes.title: Night shift work
nodes.summary: Work schedule misaligned with the circadian system. Changes when training and eating land, and lowers the recovery available from a given amount of sleep.

attrs.consequences: compressed and fragmented sleep, misaligned meal timing, variable session timing

citations: AASM practice parameters - shift work disorder (2007)

nodes.title: Prefers swimming
nodes.summary: A stated preference for swimming. Preference is a legitimate modifier, not a concession - a moderately effective intervention performed for years beats an optimal one abandoned in a month.

attrs.rationale: adherence is an axis of effectiveness, not a soft consideration

citations: Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position
US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)

nodes.title: Prefers training outdoors
nodes.summary: A stated preference for outdoor activity. Raises the practical value of anything that happens outside and is worth honouring when the alternatives are close in effect.

attrs.gap_to_watch: weather dependence can create long gaps unless an indoor fallback exists

citations: US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)

nodes.title: Prefers training at home
nodes.summary: A stated preference for home-based training. Overlaps with the no-gym constraint but is a choice rather than a limit, so the substitutions are the same and the framing is not.
citations: US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)
ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021)

nodes.title: Dislikes running
nodes.summary: A stated aversion to running. Running has no property that other modalities cannot supply - only impact loading is genuinely harder to replace, and that has strength substitutes.

attrs.note: the one thing not fully replaceable is bone loading; cover it with impact or resistance work

citations: US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee Report (2018)
Attia, Outlive (2023) - author position

nodes.title: Chest pain on exertion
nodes.summary: Chest discomfort, pressure or arm and jaw pain brought on by effort and relieved by rest. Until evaluated, this is not a training-planning problem.

attrs.urgency: urgent - same-day or emergency assessment if pain is present at rest or new

citations: AHA/ACSM joint position - exercise and acute cardiovascular events (2007)
ACSM preparticipation health screening algorithm (2015)

nodes.title: Fainting or near-fainting with exertion
nodes.summary: Loss or near-loss of consciousness during or immediately after effort. Needs cardiac evaluation before any exertion plan exists.
citations: AHA/ACSM joint position - exercise and acute cardiovascular events (2007)
ACSM preparticipation health screening algorithm (2015)

nodes.title: Unexplained weight loss
nodes.summary: Unintended loss of body weight without a change in intake or activity. Needs a diagnosis before anything is prescribed that would push weight lower.

attrs.threshold_context: commonly flagged at >5% of body weight over 6-12 months

citations: ACSM preparticipation health screening algorithm (2015)

nodes.title: New neurological deficit
nodes.summary: New weakness, numbness, loss of coordination or speech or vision change. Needs assessment; no exercise plan is the right first response.
citations: NICE NG59 low back pain and sciatica
ACSM preparticipation health screening algorithm (2015)

nodes.title: Cauda equina symptoms
nodes.summary: Saddle numbness, new bladder or bowel dysfunction, or progressive bilateral leg weakness with back pain. A surgical emergency where delay costs function permanently.

attrs.urgency: emergency - same-day imaging and surgical assessment

citations: NICE NG59 and spinal surgical society standards - cauda equina emergency
